items.when: After the Old Town sunset walk
items.name: Heart of Batumi
items.note: 4.6★ across 5,545 reviews - the broadest, most reliable Georgian menu in the city. Your orientation dinner in the neighborhood you actually like.

items.when: Work day · stay local, low effort
items.name: Tanini
items.note: 4.6★, five minutes from your door, open till midnight. Pkhali and badrijani are the light order; mtsvadi if you want protein without a heavy sauce.

items.when: After the Botanical Garden - eat on the way back
items.name: Blue Wave
items.note: Fish market row, north of the center. Pick your fish, they grill it. You'll be coming down the coast anyway.

items.when: Mountain day - eat up there, drink back here
items.name: Riverside, Makhuntseti
items.note: 4.8★, riverside, open-fire cooking and river trout at roughly half Batumi prices. Then Mahzen back in town: expat pub run by two Americans, board game night from 7pm.

items.when: Old Town office day - make this the good one
items.name: Brasserie 1900
items.note: 4.8★ and the best-reviewed proper restaurant in the city. Smart casual fits better than athleisure here, no formal requirement. Closes 23:00, and August fills it, so reserve.

items.name: Adjarian Khachapuri
items.note: Same day as Brasserie 1900, as LUNCH. Cash only, self-service, locals. The boat-shaped egg-and-butter one. It's a meal in itself, which is why it's lunch and not dinner. Closes 21:00.

items.when: Services + slack · light, near home, early night
items.name: Tanini or Sakhli
items.note: 4.7★ across 790 reviews for Sakhli. Tanini if you want the 5-minute walk. Sakhli if you want one more good night out: converted old house with a hidden courtyard and pond, gastropub menu, open till midnight.

items.name: Flight day: FlyOne 3F 588 at 12:40
items.note: Booked: FlyOne 3F 588, Batumi to Yerevan, departs 12:40, lands 14:00. Be at Batumi airport (BUS) by 10:40, which means a Bolt from home around 10:05 (about 25 minutes south). That leaves a proper breakfast at home but no farewell lunch; if you want one last khachapuri, make it a takeaway for the airport. Nothing at the airport is worth eating.

items.name: At the Sisters
items.note: (Parnavaz Mepe). 4.8★, 1,169 reviews, Ukrainian. The borscht is the draw. Closes 22:00, so this is an early-dinner option only.

items.name: Savane
items.note: (Gogebashvili). 4.8★, till midnight, quieter and less touristed than the Piazza edge. Steak and cocktails.

items.name: RETRO, Gogebashvili location
items.note: (4.3★, sea view, till 02:00). Note there are two Retros; the Takaishvili one is inland and scores lower. Reviews at both flag aggressive drink upselling: one guest was charged 40 GEL for a "homemade lemonade." Ask prices before ordering anything off-menu.

items.name: Ponte
items.note: Pizza, 4.8★, till 02:00, ~10 min from you. The non-Georgian night.

items.name: Lavanda
items.note: Literally your street. Cheap Georgian. 15% service charge and at least one report of a padded bill, so check it.

items.name: Khinkali & Chacha
items.note: 4.8★, till 01:00. Best khinkali in town if you want another round, see the note below first.

items.name: European Square Restaurant
items.note: On the Piazza: square-premium pricing, ordinary food. Decided against. Also skipping Sami Ludi's neighbors on the fish row (15% auto service charge).

items.name: Nord Specialty Coffee
items.note: Zhordania St. Shavi beans out of Tbilisi. Americano ~11, V60 ~14. Small room, 09:00-22:00.

items.name: Kopi Specialty Roasters
items.note: Lermontov St. Roasts in house, 4.8★, does breakfast. The best morning work spot of the three.

items.name: Urban Roastery
items.note: Melikishvili. Opens 08:00, earliest of the three, which matters on a work morning.

items.name: Global Coffee
items.note: (Abashidze Ave). Opens 08:00, central, fine for a work block.

items.name: Coffeetopia
items.note: Was Plan A in v1; it's 4.2★ and has become a tourist café. Use it for the view, not the coffee.

items.name: Thone bakeries
items.note: Clay-oven neighborhood bakeries, 2-5 GEL for fresh bread or khachapuri on the walk out. Daytime only.

items.name: Locus
items.note: 4.8★, bookable desks online, free coffee. Gorgasali St near the port, 20 min walk to Old Town, not in it. Closed Sat & Sun, which rules out your arrival and departure days.

items.name: LendSpace
items.note: Sherif Khimshiashvili, 4 minutes from your door and open every day 10:00-22:00, with private rooms for calls. Reviews flag weak ventilation. This is your 7-day fallback if the apartment wifi disappoints.

items.name: Vataga
items.note: (Komakhidze, 5 min from Piazza). Coworking plus board-game club, cheap, well-liked. Opens at noon weekdays, 14:00 Saturday, kills your morning.

items.name: Terminal Batumi
items.note: (Akhmeteli 7a). The only true coworking inside the Old Town footprint, open 09:00-21:00 daily including weekends, ~40 GEL. But reviews consistently describe broken AC and 30-40 Mbps. In August the AC is the dealbreaker.

items.name: D Block @ Rooms Hotel
items.note: 24/7, central, 20 GEL a visit. It's a hotel lobby with rolling suitcases. Emergency only.

items.name: Kopi or Global Coffee
items.note: For a morning work block with no day pass.

items.name: Batumi Botanical Garden
items.note: Cliffside over the sea, one of the largest in the former USSR. 2-3 hrs, hilly. Official price is 20; recent visitors report 25. Bolt ~10-20 GEL each way. Go 09:00-10:00, August afternoons are brutal on those slopes.

items.name: Makhuntseti + Adjara valley
items.note: 12th-century arched Queen Tamar bridge, waterfall, family wineries. ~1 hr inland, 10-15°C cooler and dry, the answer to "Batumi is bigger than I expected." Entry free, 2 GEL parking. Marshrutka #77 from the Old Batumi bus station on Mayakovsky runs hourly toward Keda; a hired Bolt driver for the day gives you the wineries a bus can't.

items.name: Argo Cable Car
items.note: Best panorama in the city, and better value than the Alphabet Tower deck. 2.6km, ~15 min each way, round trip included, buy online to skip a queue that runs 20 min at peak. Tickets valid 6 months. The official site warns that taxi drivers quote false prices at the lower station; ignore them. Listings disagree on closing (22:30 vs midnight), check the site the day you go.

items.name: Batumi Boulevard
items.note: 7km promenade. Seaward path the whole way, water on one side, lit towers on the other. The 4km walk from Miracle Park back to Orbi is ~50 min and the best free thing in the city.

items.name: Ali & Nino
items.note: Two steel figures pass through each other on a ~10 min cycle. Sunset. Ferris wheel 100m away, 10 GEL, runs till 01:00.

items.name: Gonio Fortress
items.note: Roman-era ruins 20 min south. 45-60 min visit. Marshrutka 1.5-2 GEL, Bolt ~20-25. Guide +25. Closes 18:00.

items.name: View Park / "WHERE" sculpture
items.note: 2km south of you, 4.8★, fountains and skate park. Good morning walk, free. Turn around at Metro City mall.

items.name: Breakwater pier by the lighthouse
items.note: (North end of Miracle Park). City skyline from the water side. Free, and a better shot than the paid decks.

items.name: Alphabet Tower deck
items.note: 20 GEL. Cut it. The cable car gives you more for 33.

items.name: Aquapark Beach
items.note: 700m south. Walk past it. Reviews describe untreated outflows nearby: smell, murky water. Decided against.

items.name: 360 Sky Bar
items.note: Great view from the right table, ordinary from the rest, and they won't seat you well unless you ask on arrival. Drink, not dinner.

items.name: Casinos
items.note: Free entry for foreigners, some comp drinks. Not a priority per your notes.

items.name: OkTopUs Gym
items.note: Sherif Khimshiashvili, 24/7, 4.5★, day passes, ~10 min walk.

items.name: Harmony Laundry
items.note: Same day, WhatsApp when ready. One reviewer got a week and a half done for 50 GEL. Far cheaper than any hotel. Do this Friday morning.

items.name: Infinity
items.note: (Kostava, 4.9★, 511 reviews). Thai massage. Roughly half what the Hilton and Sheraton spas charge for the same hour.

items.name: Siam
items.note: (Chavchavadze, 5.0★, 427 reviews). Thai massage. Roughly half what the Hilton and Sheraton spas charge for the same hour.

items.name: Barber Karalidze
items.note: (Tavdadebuli). Most central, ~25-40 GEL. Men Zone and Barbershop DIDI score higher but are well south.

items.name: Heaven Nails
items.note: Central pedicure, 4.8★.

items.name: Willmart
items.note: (Inasaridze). 24h grocery, 4.3★, better than the Magniti next door.

items.name: Grooming can wait for Yerevan
items.note: Cheaper there with more options.

items.name: Saturday departure: RESOLVED, flying
items.note: Decided and BOOKED: FlyOne 3F 588 departs Batumi 12:40, lands Yerevan 14:00 on Sat 15. About an hour and a half in the air instead of the 18-hour train-plus-bus haul via Tbilisi. Bolt to the airport around 10:05, at BUS by 10:40. You land with the whole Saturday afternoon and evening ahead of you in Yerevan.

items.name: Work window
items.note: The old version assumed you work until ~10pm Batumi time, so every dinner was a 9pm pick. This week you've been out at 8pm. The plan below assumes work mornings, explore afternoons, dinner 7-9pm. If that's wrong, the late-friendly options are flagged.

items.name: On dinner flexibility
items.note: Nothing here closes on a specific weekday. The real constraints are early-closers and weekend crowding, both flagged.

items.name: On khinkali
items.note: You had it in Tbilisi and it sat badly. That's common and not a you-problem: khinkali is a dense fistful of fatty meat and broth in thick boiled dough, usually eaten five or six at a time, and it's heavy going down. If you want the experience again, order three, not six, take the mushroom or cheese filling instead of the meat, and don't pair it with beer. Otherwise the pkhali / badrijani / grilled-meat route you've been on works better for you, and the cheese boards are doing you no harm at all.

items.name: On the coffee scene
items.note: The specialty scene here is better than "thin." These three are the real ones.

items.name: On websites
items.note: Only three places in this guide have a real one: Brasserie 1900, Locus, and Argo. Everything else in Batumi runs on Facebook or Instagram, or has no web presence at all, so those cards get a Call pill instead. That is normal here and not a quality signal: Adjarian Khachapuri is cash-only with no phone and it is one of the best things you will eat this week. Where booking matters, calling beats messaging, staff generally speak enough English and same-day reservations are easy.

items.name: The rhythm
items.note: Work mornings from the apartment or LendSpace, beach or boulevard midday, Bolt into Old Town late afternoon, dinner, walk or Bolt back. One trip into the center per day rather than fighting the 2.2km each way.

items.name: Cash
items.note: 200-300 GEL covers beach chairs, the khachapuri place, marshrutkas, and Bolt tips. TBC/BoG ATMs on Abashidze and the Boulevard. Tbilisi GEL carries over.

items.name: Tourist overcharging
items.note: Tourist overcharging is systemic here. Multiple reviews across supermarkets, beach clubs, and restaurants describe wrong change, shelf-tag mismatches, and foreigner pricing. Watch the register display, keep receipts, count change. Restaurant service charges of 10-15% are often added automatically, check before tipping again.

items.name: Beach
items.note: Pebble, not sand. Chacos are fine for walking in; they float off if you swim. All Georgian coastline is public, "private beach" doesn't exist, you're only ever renting a lounger (10-20 GEL independent, ~60 GEL at Iveria Beach). Real rip currents and patchy lifeguard coverage; respect red flags.

items.name: Weekend crowding
items.note: Old Town and the Piazza fill after 20:00 in August, especially Fri-Sat. Go at 19:00 or expect a wait. Brasserie 1900 is the only Plan A pick that genuinely needs a reservation.
